Convert from native parameters to the congruence–bias parameterisation

Source: R/mfd.R
dpars_to_mfd.Rd

Converts from the native parameters (the rates mu, lambdaone, and lambdatwo) to the congruence–bias parameterisation (the midpoint M of the two expected counts, the congruence f, and the source bias delta), and, optionally, converts native dispersions (shapes, shapex, shapexone, and shapextwo) to overdispersions (kappas, kappax, kappaxone, and kappaxtwo). mfd_to_dpars() converts in the other direction.

Usage

dpars_to_mfd(
  mu,
  lambdaone,
  lambdatwo,
  shapes = NULL,
  shapex = NULL,
  shapexone = NULL,
  shapextwo = NULL
)

Arguments

mu

Rate of the shared component.

lambdaone, lambdatwo

Rates of the source-1-exclusive and source-2-exclusive components.

shapes, shapex

Optional NB2 (inverse) dispersion parameters. Supplying shapes adds kappas = 1/sqrt(shapes) to the returned list, so shapes = Inf gives kappas = 0. A binegbin fit made before 0.10.0 has one dispersion, shapex, for both exclusive components; supplying shapex adds kappax. For bipois() and bipois_partialobs(), which have no dispersion parameters, leave every dispersion argument unset.

shapexone, shapextwo

Optional NB2 (inverse) dispersion parameters of the two exclusive components. Supplying them adds kappaxone and kappaxtwo to the returned list. Mutually exclusive with shapex.

Value

A named list of M, f, delta, and beta = tanh(delta), the source bias on a scale bounded by -1 and 1, with kappas, kappax, kappaxone, and kappaxtwo added when the corresponding dispersions are supplied.

Details

Each argument may be a vector, such as the posterior draws of the rates. mu, lambdaone, and lambdatwo are recycled to the length of the longest of the three, and any dispersions to the same length; each element of the returned list is a vector of that length.

Rates of exactly zero, which posterior draws do not produce, give values that are not finite: delta is NA when both exclusive rates are zero, and Inf or -Inf when one of them is, and f is NA when M is zero.

See also

mfd_to_dpars(), bipois(), bipois_partialobs(), binegbin(), binegbin_partialobs()

Examples

dpars_to_mfd(mu = 8.04, lambdaone = 4.75, lambdatwo = 3.17)
#> $M
#> [1] 12
#> 
#> $f
#> [1] 0.67
#> 
#> $delta
#> [1] 0.2022065
#> 
#> $beta
#> [1] 0.1994949
#> 

# Round trip
d <- mfd_to_dpars(M = 12, f = 0.67, delta = 0.2)
dpars_to_mfd(d$mu, d$lambdaone, d$lambdatwo)[c("M", "f", "delta")]
#> $M
#> [1] 12
#> 
#> $f
#> [1] 0.67
#> 
#> $delta
#> [1] 0.2
#> 

# Perfect congruence: delta cannot be recovered and is returned as NA
dpars_to_mfd(mu = 12, lambdaone = 0, lambdatwo = 0)$delta
#> [1] NA
